To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the ethical values that have been developed over the years by archivists and libraries can and should be applied to the algorithms that will take care of many of their tasks in the future.

(1) the physical world is being digitalized; (2) the digital world is being algorithmized; (3) the ethical codes of archives, libraries and museums can be used to guide the algorithmization of digital archives, libraries and museum.

“The future of archives, libraries, museums and related institutions, in the context of the algorithmic turn, is to be codementalists: algorithmic documentalistic experts that ensure that algorithms behave according to the ethical norms of society.”
In summary, our research is concerned with
the ethics of algorithms and how to ensure they will behave according to our human ethical norms.
the ethical aspects of the algorithmization of archiving and library science.
the ethical principles that should guide algorithmization and digitalization, and how these should be implemented in code of ethics and algorithms.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
“The ethics of algorithms in archival institutions is a new research field that requires interdisciplinary research and development, and in which archival science can make a valuable contribution.”
the ethics of algorithms in archivists, librarians and society are a new and important research field that requires a multidisciplinary approach.
we need to develop algorithms that obey human ethical values, and we need to develop human ethical values that obey algorithms.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we are developing a framework to ensure that algorithms that will take-over many of our familiar tasks in archives, libraries, and museums, will behave according our human ethical norms that evolved over many years.
the ethical values of archives and libraries are not static but dynamic and that the ethical values are changing in the context of algorithmization.
in the age of algorithms we need to understand the human ethical values that are encoded in our code of ethics, and then encode those in our code for algorithms.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ethical codes can be formalized in the form of logical theories.
the ethical values of archivists, librarians and documentalists can be formalized in the form of an ethical code, and that these ethical values can be encoded in the form of algorithms.
ethical principles, as expressed in ethical codes, can be used to design and implement ethical algorithms.
